text.p: The following stories were reported in Lithuanian newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Christian Democrats do not want to be a younger brother in the coalition with the Homeland Union. The coalition partners differ in their opinion on the state's stake in Butinges, privatisation of big enterprises in the communication, transport and energy sectors and alcohol and tobacco control.
- The election comission decided to held run-off elections for two vacant seats in parliament on March 22, 1998.

- Vilniaus Bank, Hermis Bank, Nomura International, Hansapank and the Lithuanian Credit Union Limited submitted letters to the finance ministry showing their interest to participate in the privatisation of the troubled state-run Lithuanian Commercial bank.
- Vilfima was the most active broker on the stock exchange during the first quarter of 1997, accounting for 22.26 percent of bourse turnover.
- Representatives of Russian oil company Jukos are to arrive in Lithuania today to meet Economy Minister Vincas Babilius and the representatives of the country's oil sector.
- Lithuania denies it has signed an agreement with NATO which allows alliance aircrafts to monitor the territory of Kaliningrad from Lithuanian territory.
- The chairman of the board of Siauliu Bank Zenonas Sabalys said he learned about the intentions of Hermis Bank to acquire a controlling stake in his bank from the mass media.
- The representatives of Ford forecast that in 1997 2,700 new Western cars will be sold in Lithuania and 10 percent will be Fords.
- European Affairs Minister Laima Andrikiene told the newspaper that applications to draw up a privatisation program for Lithuanian Telecom are expected before May 9.
- Andrikiene said during a meeting with Danish businessmen in Copenhagen that Danish firms should take part in Lithuania's privatisation programme.
- Danish Borsen newspaper forecast that Danish investments into Lithuania may reach one billion DKK in 1997.
- Preliminary data shows that Snoras bank had around 5 million litas of net profit in the first quarter of 1997.
